name: Jordan Avery
summary: Marketing analytics leader who builds measurement functions from scratch and connects marketing spend to revenue. Two sentences at most; the pipeline rewrites this per posting.
positioning_notes: Lead with measurement and experimentation, not channel management. Prefer roles where the analytics function is being built rather than maintained.
differentiator: Builds the measurement practice and the models, rather than managing vendors who do.

work_history.title: Head of Marketing Analytics
work_history.company_descriptor: DTC home goods retailer, ~$400M revenue, ~$90M annual ad spend. NOTE: this field describes the EMPLOYER, not what you personally worked on. The pipeline is told never to turn these markets into your accomplishments.
highlights: Built the marketing measurement function from a standing start, hiring and developing a team of five analysts.
Deployed Bayesian marketing mix models across eight channels, shifting $12M of annual spend and lifting contribution margin 9%.
Designed geo-holdout incrementality tests that corrected a 40% overstatement in last-click attribution for paid social.
Developed a predictive LTV model that reset acquisition bidding, increasing marginal profit on ad spend 22%.
Established metric definitions and data quality standards adopted across marketing, finance, and product.

work_history.title: Manager, Marketing Analytics
work_history.company_descriptor: Independent media agency, ~$120M billings, clients across retail, travel, and financial services.
highlights: Built attribution and media models governing roughly $75M in annual client media budgets.
Automated weekly client reporting, cutting analyst production time 60% and freeing the team for analysis.
Ran the agency's experimentation program, including a test archive that stopped teams repeating known failures.

work_history.title: Senior Research Analyst
work_history.company_descriptor: Market research firm specializing in consumer packaged goods.
highlights: Designed and fielded syndicated survey research with annual samples above 20,000 respondents.
Introduced conjoint analysis to the product portfolio, creating a new revenue line for the firm.
